chunks: Al-Nawfali, from al-Sakawni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a man who had been struck, so part of his speech was lost and part remained. He set his blood-money (diyah) according to the letters of the alphabet (al-mu'jam). Then he said: 'Speak the alphabet; whatever is missing from his speech is calculated accordingly.' The alphabet consists of twenty-eight letters, so he made twenty-eight parts; whatever is missing from that is calculated accordingly.

key_terms.حُرُوفُ الْمُعْجَمِ: Letters of the alphabet (specifically the 28 classical Arabic letters)

ai.seo_question: How is the blood money calculated for someone who has lost their ability to speak clearly?
ai.summary: In this foundational juristic precedent from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) established a precise quantitative methodology for *diyah* (blood-money) by equating the loss of speech to the loss of the twenty-eight letters of the Arabic alphabet. This ruling demonstrates the application of proportional compensation (*nisab*) in Shia fiqh, where the total *diyah* is divided into twenty-eight parts, with each missing letter representing a specific fraction of the full compensation. It highlights the Imam's attention to linguistic detail as a basis for legal equity in cases of physical injury.
